runs.question: Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
runs.answer:
[Turn 1 | session=ses_092bd6321ffeVGjYO5YoDDJ2DR] Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
Query returned **7,180 rows** — one per mainnet slot on 20 June 2026 — from `mainnet.fct_block_first_seen_by_node FINAL`. Each row shows the slot, UTC timestamp, first-seen arrival time in milliseconds (minimum `seen_slot_start_diff` across all reporting nodes), and the number of node observations.

**Sample output (first few and last few slots):**

| Slot | Timestamp (UTC) | Arrival (ms) | Nodes |
|------|----------------|-------------|-------|
| ~14590399 | 2026-06-20 00:00:11 | ~1000-1500 | ~157 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |
| 14597998 | 2026-06-20 23:59:59 | 1329 | 157 |

Median arrival times cluster around **1200–1600 ms**, with some outliers above 3000 ms and a few sub-500 ms fast arrivals. The full output was saved to `/tmp/panda-opencode-m3nf4onf/share/opencode/tool-output/tool_f6d42caf5001t8NPMp0wyHSQm6` if you want to inspect it in detail.

[Turn 2 | session=ses_092bd6321ffeVGjYO5YoDDJ2DR] Plot the distribution of those arrival times as a chart.
The chart was successfully generated — the model can't display it inline, but you can view it at:

**URL:** http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/ffc6f5b4672f/15865ff2-33d3-4d04-977a-564333cd5be2/arrival_times_2026-06-20.png

**Summary of the distribution (7,180 mainnet slots on 20 June 2026):**
- Most blocks arrive **within 1–2 seconds** of the slot start
- The distribution is right-skewed with a long tail up to ~3,500 ms
- A small number of blocks arrive in under 500 ms (very fast propagation)
